title: The Unicorn Horn Throne Was Actually Made of Narwhal Tusks
hook: The chair Danish kings used for their accession rites was made from narwhal tusks that were called unicorn horn

open.title: A king's chair was called unicorn horn, but the real material was something else
open.line: A castle in Denmark has a king's chair said to be made of unicorn horn. But there are no unicorns. What is this white horn really made of?

summary: King Frederik 3 of Denmark had a chair made from narwhal tusks, then called unicorn horn. The tusk is a tooth that grows long from the upper jaw, and the king knew it.

text: Rosenborg Castle in Denmark has a king's chair made of white horn.
Frederik 3 had it made in 1662, and it was first used in 1671, at the next king's ceremony.
He chose something more precious than ivory: unicorn horn.
Back then, Europeans believed unicorn horn protected against poison.
In fact, that horn was the tusk of the narwhal, a whale of the northern seas.
And a tusk isn't a horn either. It's a canine tooth that grows long from the left side of the upper jaw.
It can be 1.5 to 3 meters long.
According to the Royal Danish Collection, the king knew full well that this was narwhal tusk.
Even so, the chair was handed down with the story that it was made of unicorn horn.
